# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 8 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_008_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 8

**8:1** And her parents went down marveling and praising and glorifying the Lord God, because the child did not turn back. And Mary remained in the temple of the Lord like a dove being nurtured, and she received food from the hand of an angel.

**8:2** And when she was twelve years old there was held a council of the priests, saying: "Behold, Mary has completed twelve years in the temple of the Lord our God. What then shall we do with her, that she may not defile the sanctuary of the Lord our God?"

**8:3** And they said to the high priest: "You stand at the altar of the Lord. Go in and pray concerning her, and whatever the Lord God reveals to you, this we will do."

**8:4** And the high priest took the vestment with twelve bells and went into the Holy of Holies and prayed concerning her. And behold, an angel of the Lord appeared, saying to him: "Zechariah, Zechariah, go out and assemble the widowers of the people, and let them each bring a staff, and to whomsoever the Lord God shows a sign, his wife she shall be."

**8:5** And heralds went out through all the surrounding country of Judea, and the trumpet of the Lord sounded, and all came running together.

---

## Translator's Note

The high priest named here as Zechariah is likely the same Zechariah, father of John the Baptist, who is killed in chapter 23 — the author is creating narrative coherence. The motif of the "vestment with twelve bells" is priestly realism (cf. Exod 28:33-35). Mary's description as a "dove nurtured in the temple" (8:1) has been the basis for calling the dove a symbol of Mary in Christian art. The assembly of widowers with staffs anticipates the Staff Miracle in chapter 9.
